Priya Patel: Quick sync — SOC2 launch question. Customer A asked for an exception path for audit log retention (they need 7 years for certain tenants). We need concrete launch acceptance criteria and a recommended MVP implementation.
Samir Gupta: Can you share the exact ask? full searchable retention or just archival export?
Priya Patel: They said searchable events for compliance review, but willing to accept slower access. Product preference is default 1 year searchable and archival beyond that.
Miguel Torres: From Legal: if we offer an exception, it must be in contract (explicit retention extension + indemnity for data residency). Also need proof-of-integrity for any archived exports (signed manifest + checksums).
Anita Chen: Ops note: keeping 7y searchable per-tenant has ~5x storage and index cost. Cold-only archival (object store) ok, but reindex-on-demand will add compute spikes. Need to be explicit about search SLA.
Samir Gupta: Technical options: 1) Keep full index for 7y (expensive) 2) Archive raw events + keep lightweight metadata index (cheaper, limited search) 3) Store full raw and provide on-demand reindexing pipeline (latency tradeoff). For MVP I'd push option 3 with documented export integrity.
Priya Patel: Proposed MVP acceptance criteria:
- Documented exception process and approval flow
- Contract addendum template for retention extensions
- Archival export facility that produces a signed manifest + checksum
- Exports respect tenant BYOK when enabled (archive encrypted with tenant key)
- Ops SLA: export available within 48 hours for archival retrieval
- No guaranteed full-text search beyond 1 year in MVP (can reindex on request, billed)
Miguel Torres: Legal ok with that shape, but insist: signed manifest must include hash algo and UTC timestamps. Also require audit trail of who triggered exports.
Anita Chen: Ops: 48h export SLA seems doable for launch if we limit concurrency. Need a runbook and billing code. I'll estimate cost impact and propose pricing tiers.
Samir Gupta: Implementation notes: reindex-on-demand implies we must snapshot raw events with schema version metadata. Recommend storing object with key pattern: tenant/<tenant-id>/audit/<yyyy-mm>/chunk-<uuid>.gz and manifest JSON. Also add header: "x-retention-policy: extended". We'll need KMS changes for BYOK — if tenant BYOK, use tenant key to encrypt archive; if not, use platform key.
Priya Patel: Action items:
- Samir: prototype archival export + signed manifest + BYOK encryption flow
- Anita: ops cost estimate + runbook + pricing proposal
- Miguel: contract addendum + compliance wording
- Priya: draft acceptance checklist and pilot invite to Customer A
ops-bot: RFC assigned: RFC-2023-47 (retention-exceptions). Please link PRs to RFC.
Samir Gupta: One more: rotation/escrow edgecase — if tenant rotates keys or revokes, we need access policy for archived data. Will include rotation handling in prototype.
Miguel Torres: Legal asks that reindexing compute be explicitly chargeable and opt-in in contract. I'll add phrasing.
Anita Chen: Will add a note: "If reindex requested, customer bears compute cost unless pre-paid tier" — needed for approval.
Priya Patel: OK — scheduling follow-up Friday 11:00 PT to review prototype and acceptance checklist. @Samir @Anita @Miguel add blockers here. :thumbsup:
Miguel Torres: Added contract questions in thread. One open question: do we tie extended-retention offers to SOC2/ISO-only customers or make generally available? Legal prefers limit to contract customers for now.
Priya Patel: Good point — we'll scope pilot to enterprise contracts only. I'll reflect that in the acceptance doc and pilot invite.
